rationale_summary: The AI RMF FAQs are dominantly framed around innovation_enablement, presenting a voluntary, scalable, non-mandatory standards framework aimed at fostering innovative approaches to trustworthiness, improving measurement science, and building confidence in AI systems. Innovation_enablement leads consumer_public_safety, which is a strong runner-up focused on managing AI risks to individuals, organizations, society, and quality of life through safe, valid, and reliable systems. Economic_competitiveness ('enhance economic security') and fundamental_rights ('privacy-enhanced, and fair with harmful bias managed') serve as clear secondary frames, with a minor national_security nod to NSCAI recommendations.

evidence_spans.quote: NIST is developing forward-thinking approaches that support innovation and confidence in AI systems.
evidence_spans.source_section: Will NIST provide additional guidance to help with using the AI RMF?

evidence_spans.quote: It aims to foster the development of innovative approaches to address characteristics of trustworthiness including valid and reliable, safe, secure and resilient, accountable and transparent, explainable and interpretable, privacy-enhanced, and fair with harmful bias managed.
The Framework is intended to help developers, users and evaluators of AI systems better manage AI risks which could affect individuals, organizations, society, or the environment.
NIST aims to cultivate trust in the design, development, use, and evaluation of AI technologies and systems in ways that enhance economic security and improve quality of life.
